course.title: Debating and Argumentation
course.tagline: Argue any point with logic, evidence and calm confidence.

days.title: What is a debate?
days.goal: Say what a debate is and how it works.

video.title: How to write a debate in seven easy steps

steps: Watch today's video and write down the main technique for what a debate is: two sides, one motion, a judge in your own words.
Write a short for-and-against list on today's topic, using what a debate is: two sides, one motion, a judge.
Practise arguing one side of what a debate is: two sides, one motion, a judge aloud for 3 minutes, then switch sides.
Write a one-paragraph rebuttal to the strongest point on the other side.
Debate what a debate is: two sides, one motion, a judge with a friend or family member for 5 minutes today.
days.task: Write down what a debate is in two sentences.
days.challenge: Explain a debate to a friend in one minute.

quiz.q: What is a debate?
options: Two sides argue for and against one idea, and a judge picks the winner.
Two people shouting at each other.
One person talking alone.
A test with right and wrong answers.
quiz.explain: A debate has two sides, one idea to argue about (called a motion), and a judge who picks the winner.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Give a two-minute speech for one side of a motion.
Say what a debate is and how it works.
Stay calm when someone attacks your point.
Use short notes, not a full script.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about What is a debate? — its goal is: Say what a debate is and how it works.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: linking evidence to your claim
rebutting with evidence
asking good questions in debate
what a debate is: two sides, one motion, a judge
quiz.explain: Today's focus was what a debate is: two sides, one motion, a judge.

days.title: Know the motion

quiz.q: What is a motion?
options: The idea the debate is about, like 'School uniforms should be banned'.
A hand movement.
A type of speech.
The name of the judge.
quiz.explain: The motion is the idea being debated. One side supports it, the other side opposes it.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Listen and write down the other side's points.
Debate a motion for four minutes.
Understand what the motion asks you to argue.
Debate a topic with strong feelings on both sides.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Know the motion — its goal is: Understand what the motion asks you to argue.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: understanding the motion
building a full argument: claim, evidence, link
logical fallacies: tricks that make arguments bad
speaking with confidence in debate
quiz.explain: Today's focus was understanding the motion.

capstone.title: The Debater
capstone.brief: Debate a motion in front of a small audience. Give an opening speech, rebut the other side, and close with your best points. Ask the audience to judge.
checks: You stated your side clearly
You gave three arguments with evidence
You rebutted the other side's best point
You stayed calm under pressure
You closed with your best points
You spoke clearly and slowly
You asked the judge for feedback and wrote it down
deliverables: A video or audio recording of your debate
A one-page plan of your case: motion, side, three arguments, evidence
A written rebuttal of the other side's best point
A list of feedback from the judge and audience
A short note on what you will improve next
